title: Optimize CPU request path: reduce serialization overhead, pin thread pools, and improve batching scheduler
author: Ethan Collins
release_notes: Reduce CPU-side latency and P99 for short requests by optimizing serialization, pinning request thread pools to cores, and improving batching scheduler. No public API changes.
body:
Motivation: We observed CPU-side bottlenecks for short/low-token requests in the serving runtime. End-to-end traces and flamegraphs pointed to serialization (protobuf/cbor) and scheduler overhead on the request path, plus thread migration causing poor cache locality. This PR targets three complementary areas: 1) reduce redundant serialization and fast-path encode/decode, 2) pin the request processing thread pool to stable core sets to improve cache locality and reduce context-switch overhead, 3) refine the continuous batching scheduler to avoid unnecessary wakeups and reduce lock contention for small batches.

What changed: Implemented a lightweight fast-path serializer for the common streaming message shape and deferred heavy encode/alloc until after batching when possible; added a cpu_affinity option and core-set pinning for the request handler thread pool with sensible defaults per deployment tier; reworked the batching scheduler to use a token-based batching coalescer with relaxed locking for short-wait batches; improved metrics and tracing around KV cache hits to ensure batching-aware cache reuse.

Checklist: - [x] Implement fast-path serializer and integrated into request pipeline - [x] Add cpu affinity + pinning config and tests - [x] Update batching scheduler and add microbench harness - [x] Add regression guards in CI (bench + unit) - [x] Run extended perf validation on dedicated infra

Testing and validation: Unit tests added for serializer and pinning logic. New microbench harness and integration perf job (infra/ci/run-bench.yml) exercises steady-state short-request workloads. Benchmarks were run across multi-core instances and dedicated GPU nodes to ensure no regressions for long-running generation workloads. Also validated in canary: waving rollout to 5% of traffic in the hosted fleet for 48h.

Backward compatibility: No API surface changes. Feature gate controls affinity behavior and is off by default for legacy clusters.

Notes: This is focused on CPU-path efficiency and does not change GPU kernels or model execution paths. Future follow-ups will add dynamic core packing based on load and a load-aware pinning policy.

review_comments: Marina Zhao (2026-01-06): Left a few nits on allocator lifetime in fast_serializer.rs — please ensure no extra allocations on the hot path.
Ethan Collins (2026-01-07): Addressed Marina's comments; added stack-backed buffer to avoid heap alloc when payload < 2KB.

Diego Alvarez (2026-01-08): Questioned the default pinning policy on cloud VMs — we should keep this opt-in for older deployments. Suggested adding a feature gate and metric to track eviction pressure.
Ethan Collins (2026-01-09): Added "request_pool_affinity" feature flag and metric 'request_pool_migrations_total'.
Priya Raman (2026-01-11): Verified microbench harness and approved after seeing stable CI bench runs.
performance_results: Small request median tail latency (hosted, 1-8 tokens): baseline 12.6ms -> 8.1ms (≈ -35.7%)
CPU per-core utilization (steady-state short requests): baseline 72% -> 56% (-22%)
Throughput for batched short requests (64-client synthetic): baseline 1200 rps -> 2160 rps (+1.8x)
KV-cache hit churn decreased, observed 12% fewer cache invalidation-related stalls on batched path
upgrade_instructions: No required upgrade. To enable CPU pinning in Dedicated clusters set request_pool_affinity=true in the runtime config and restart the request pool process. Monitor 'request_pool_migrations_total' and the new 'request_pool_core_affinity' metric. Rollout slowly for large, multi-tenant hosts.
notes: We intentionally keep affinity off for older clouds; follow-up PR will add auto-detection of hyperthreading and NUMA-aware packing.
